clue.text: Clever device, note, in Tom Sharpe novel

indicators.note: novel means new or unusual, so the letters are formed into a new arrangement

parts.note: the comic novelist's name, taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: A reader spots a clever gadget, with a note attached, in one of Tom Sharpe's comic novels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a noun naming one of Sharpe's books, but it is the anagram signal: N put in with TOMSHARPE is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A mobile handset that runs apps and browses the web is the everyday example of a smart gadget.

clue.text: Mum's car key could be found in handbag, perhaps

definitions.text: could be found in handbag, perhaps

parts.note: Ma's, a mother's, informally
taken as written
A is a musical key

explanation.surface: Mum's car key might well be lost somewhere in her handbag.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a loose description: eyelash make-up is a typical item carried in a handbag.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyelash cosmetic is something many people carry in a handbag, hence the 'perhaps' marking an example.

clue.text: Large anchor pulled up onto prow of yacht

indicators.note: in a down entry, pulled up means the word for anchor is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to anchor a boat is to moor it

indicators.note: the prow is the front of a boat, so the opening letter of the word yacht is taken

explanation.surface: A large anchor is hauled up onto the bow of a yacht.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anchor' is the verb here: to make a boat fast. 'pulled up' signals reading upwards in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spacious with plenty of space inside is large, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Colour match in ink container

indicators.note: in places the word for match inside the word for the ink container

parts.note: a fountain pen holds ink
to agree is to match or correspond

explanation.surface: A colour that matches the shade of the ink in its container.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright yellowish-green shade is named after garden peas, so it is a colour.

clue.text: Cryptic clue in one newspaper's leader: 'a boom with extremely low frequency'

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling or encoded, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken letter for letter as fodder
the leader of the word newspaper is its first letter, N, followed by the words a boom as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper editorial runs a cryptic clue about a boom in something that hardly ever happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cryptic' rearranges CLUEINONE, N and ABOOM together; 'extremely low frequency' sounds like radio jargon, but it means very rarely.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something that happens very rarely, which is extremely low frequency.

clue.text: Journalist quits current affairs?

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist
to quit life is to die, so quits gives dies

explanation.surface: A journalist gives up covering current affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current affairs' reads as news, but it means whirls in a flowing current of water; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Swirling movements in a stream are things that happen in a current, punningly 'current affairs'.

clue.text: Figure on coin (fifty pence piece)

indicators.note: piece means a portion, so a run of letters is taken from inside the words fifty pence

explanation.surface: A design on a coin, such as on the fifty pence piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fifty pence piece' is a real British coin, but 'piece' is the signal: the letters sit across 'fifTY PEnce'.
explanation.definitionFit: In coin collecting the design or figure stamped on a coin is called its type, a specialist sense.

clue.text: Short circuit on board is easily managed

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, so the last letter of the word for circuit is dropped

parts.note: a racing circuit is a track
a board is a table, as in bed and board or a board for meals

explanation.surface: A short circuit on a circuit board turns out to be easy to fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short circuit' looks like an electrical fault; 'Short' trims TRACK to TRAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something docile and readily controlled is easily managed, a direct synonym.

clue.text: University official gets a month inside for extortion, essentially

indicators.note: inside puts the month's abbreviation within the letters for and the centre of extortion

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
OCT is short for October

indicators.note: the essence is the heart, so the central letter of the word extortion is taken

explanation.surface: A university official goes to prison for a month for extortion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' suggests jail, but it is the container signal; 'essentially' takes the single central letter of extortion.
explanation.definitionFit: At Oxford and Cambridge a disciplinary officer of the university holds this title.

clue.text: Circle Line, accordingly, goes around city

parts.note: a circle is shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: goes around means the word for accordingly surrounds the abbreviation for line

parts.note: so means therefore, accordingly

explanation.surface: The Circle Line, a London Underground route, runs round the city accordingly.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Tube line, but here it is O and L.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Norway is a city.

clue.text: Church official's mischievous, having area coned off outside

parts.note: an arch look is playfully mischievous

indicators.note: outside means the reworked letters of coned go around the abbreviation for area
off means wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: A cheeky churchman has had an area coned off outside his church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coned off' reads as traffic cones, but 'off' rearranges CONED to DECON, which goes 'outside' A. The 's in official's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior Anglican cleric ranking below a bishop is a church official.

clue.text: Brief film entertains wife

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so the word for film holds the abbreviation for wife

parts.note: a film is a thin layer

explanation.surface: A short film entertains someone's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' looks like an adjective for the film; it is the noun, British slang for a legal representative.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a brief is the legal professional who represents someone in court.

clue.text: Name of bird I refuse to eat

indicators.note: eating takes something in, so I and the word for refuse go around the bird

parts.note: to refuse is to deny
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: Someone names a bird they refuse to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's name is their identification, so it stands for who they are.

clue.text: Forged ahead, mostly, with barn dance

indicators.note: forged means made or shaped, so the letters are worked into a new order
mostly means all but the last letter of the word ahead

parts.note: taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: Someone pushed on with a lively barn dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forged ahead' reads as a phrase meaning pressed on, but 'Forged' is the anagram signal on AHEA (ahead without its last letter) and BARN.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow Cuban dance in duple time, made famous in Carmen, is a type of dance.

clue.text: A fellow, if climbing crane, supplies legal document

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing reads the word if from bottom to top

parts.note: a davit is a small crane on a ship, used for lowering boats

explanation.surface: A man climbing a crane hands over a legal document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns IF into FI.
explanation.definitionFit: A written statement sworn on oath for use in court is a legal document.

clue.text: Slight charge for refreshments — not bad

indicators.note: not means without, so the word for bad is removed

parts.note: a bar bill is what you are charged for drinks
ill means bad, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: A small charge for refreshments is not too bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slight' looks like an adjective meaning small; it is the noun, an insult.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutting remark aimed to wound is a slight, both meaning an insult.

clue.text: Scrap paper surrounds Steptoe and Son?

indicators.note: surrounds means the paper's abbreviation goes around the other piece

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times newspaper
Steptoe and Son was a British TV sitcom about a father and son who were rag-and-bone men, collectors of junk

explanation.surface: A scrap of paper is wrapped around a reference to the old sitcom Steptoe and Son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap paper' looks like one thing; 'Scrap' is the definition and 'paper' the FT.
explanation.definitionFit: A small broken-off piece is a scrap, a direct synonym.

clue.text: In fall, one dislocated thumb

definitions.meaning: a cryptic description: something that comes loose in autumn (the American fall) from a tree
to thumb a book is to turn its pages, to flick through it

explanation.surface: Someone dislocated a thumb in a fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall' looks like a tumble but is autumn; 'dislocated' means detached from a twig.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: what drops from trees in autumn, and to flick through pages with the thumb.

clue.text: An act of self-importance, say, to put up rent

parts.note: eg, for example, means say

indicators.note: in a down entry, put up reads the word to from bottom to top

parts.note: a rent is a tear, a rip

explanation.surface: Putting up the rent might be called an act of self-importance by a landlord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like money paid; it is a tear. 'put up' turns TO into OT.
explanation.definitionFit: An activity pursued to boost one's own vanity is an act of self-importance.

clue.text: Superman's motive, it's said, is philanthropy

indicators.note: it's said means the phrase is spoken, so its sound gives the entry

parts.note: the motif on Superman's chest is a large letter S, so the words give large S

explanation.surface: Superman's driving purpose is said to be love of humanity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'motive' stands for motif: the big S on Superman's costume.
explanation.definitionFit: Generous giving of money or gifts is the practical form of philanthropy.

clue.text: Yes, six volts is maintained — it's live

indicators.note: something maintained is held, so the word for yes holds the other letters

parts.note: sure means yes, certainly
VI is six in Roman numerals
V is the symbol for volts

explanation.surface: An electrician confirms that six volts is kept on the wire, so it's live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'live' looks like an electrical term for a charged wire; it is the verb, to stay alive.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on existing or remain alive is to live, a direct synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Talk about soldier going north then south in cutter

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for talk goes around the soldier and south

parts.note: to jaw is to talk at length

indicators.note: in a down entry, going north reads the soldier's letters from bottom to top

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A conversation about a soldier sailing north and then south in a cutter, a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutter' looks like a sailing boat; it is a saw that cuts curves.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine-bladed saw for cutting curved shapes is a cutter, a tool that cuts.

clue.text: Volley first struck shoulder

indicators.note: first struck means the opening letter is struck out

parts.note: a broadside is a volley of fire from all guns on one side of a ship

explanation.surface: A volley of shots struck someone's shoulder first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoulder' looks like part of the body; it is the verge beside a road.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard shoulder or verge alongside a carriageway is the strip at the side of a road.

clue.text: Worry about test for supporting metal framework

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word for worry is read backwards

parts.note: to nag is to worry or pester
a try is a test or attempt

explanation.surface: Someone frets over a test of a supporting metal framework.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridge-like steel structure that carries cranes, signals or rockets is a supporting metal framework.

clue.text: Broadcast only new material

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A broadcaster airs only new material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' suggests content; it is a fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A synthetic polymer fabric used for stockings is a material, an example of a textile.

clue.text: German veterans assembled around old memorial

indicators.note: around means the reworked letters of veterans go round the abbreviation for old
assembled means put together, so the letters are put together in a new order

parts.note: taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: German veterans gathered around an old war memorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembled' rearranges VETERANS around O.
explanation.definitionFit: A headstone over a grave is a memorial to the person buried there.

clue.text: Call round for set

indicators.note: round means turned about, so the word for call is read backwards

parts.note: to dial is to call on the telephone

explanation.surface: A call goes round for a set.
explanation.definitionFit: To have set something down is to have placed it, so the past tense of lay means set.

clue.text: Notice jam stain

definitions.meaning: to notice something is to see or catch sight of it
a jam is a tight situation, a predicament
a stain is a mark or blemish

explanation.surface: Notice the jam stain on the tablecloth.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: 'jam stain' reads as a single mark, but 'jam' is a predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: Each sense fits: to see, a tight situation (in a tricky one), and a small mark or blemish.

clue.text: In here, might model meet biggest fan?

definitions.text: In here, might model meet biggest fan?

parts.words: In here, might model meet biggest fan?
parts.note: a model aircraft or car is tested here, facing a huge fan that blows air at it; the surface suggests a fashion model and an admirer

explanation.surface: A celebrity model might encounter their greatest admirer here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' and 'fan' suggest celebrity; read them as a scale model and a blower.
explanation.definitionFit: Engineers test scale models in an enclosed tube where giant fans blow air over them.
